Latest Money stories

Money

Wed Nov 11mortgages

Mortgage rates jump to 7.30% after the inflation report, ending four weeks of declines

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose 12 basis points on Tuesday to 7.30%, its biggest one-day jump in more than a month, after a hotter-than-expected consumer price report, CNBC reported, citing Mortgage News Daily.

Wed Nov 11economy

Fed officials signal more rate hikes after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report

Several Federal Reserve officials called for further interest rate increases after consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, with Governor Christopher Waller saying a half-point hike should be considered in December if core inflation came in around 0.3%, as it did, according to his speech and CNBC.

Tue Nov 10economy

U.S. household debt rises to $19.1 trillion as credit card balances hit a record $1.29 trillion

Total U.S. household debt rose by $334 billion, or 1.8%, in the third quarter to $19.1 trillion, with credit card balances up $22 billion to a record $1.29 trillion, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said on Tuesday.

Tue Nov 10economy

About 1 in 4 Americans with a credit record has debt in collections, Urban Institute finds

About 23.5% of Americans with a credit history have debt in collections, with a median amount of $2,913, according to a new Urban Institute analysis reported by Business Insider and CBS News.

Mon Nov 9economy

New York Fed survey: inflation expectations hold at 3.9% as unemployment worries hit highest since 2020

Median U.S. consumer inflation expectations were unchanged in October at 3.9% one year ahead, 3.3% three years ahead and 3.0% five years ahead, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said Monday in its Survey of Consumer Expectations.

Mon Nov 9energy

U.S. average gas price falls below $4 a gallon for the first time since August, GasBuddy says

The U.S. average price of gasoline fell to about $3.96 a gallon on Monday, down nearly 16 cents over the past week and below $4 for the first time since August, according to GasBuddy data cited by MarketWatch.

Fri Nov 6economy

Consumer credit jumps at 6.4% annual pace in September as revolving borrowing surges

U.S. consumer credit rose at a 6.4% seasonally adjusted annual rate in September, lifting outstanding balances by about $27.8 billion to $5.22 trillion, the Federal Reserve said Friday.

Fri Nov 6economy

U.S. average gas price slips to $4.07, down about 14 cents in a week

The national average price for regular gasoline fell to $4.0688 a gallon as of Friday, down from $4.2046 a week earlier, according to AAA fuel-price data.

Fri Nov 6economy

Credit-card balances hit $1.16 trillion as more cardholders fall 90 days behind

U.S. bankcard balances rose 4.5% year over year to $1.16 trillion in the third quarter, while the share of cardholders 90 or more days past due climbed to 2.50%, TransUnion said in a report released Wednesday.

Thu Nov 5mortgages

30-year mortgage rate falls to 7.18%, a third straight weekly drop

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate fell to 7.18% this week from 7.24%, its third consecutive weekly decline, Freddie Mac said Thursday.

Thu Nov 5economy

Weekly jobless claims fall to 189,000 as four-week average also drops

First-time claims for state unemployment benefits fell by 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 189,000 in the week ended Oct. 31, the Labor Department said Thursday.

Thu Nov 5economy

Worker productivity rises 3.6% in Q3 as unit labor costs fall 0.7%

Nonfarm business labor productivity rose at a 3.6% annualized rate in the third quarter as output increased 3.7% and hours worked edged up 0.1%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Thursday.

Mon Nov 2economy

Gas prices fall 17.1 cents in a week to a $4.12 average, GasBuddy says

The U.S. average price of gasoline fell 17.1 cents over the past week to $4.12 a gallon, GasBuddy said Monday, while AAA put its national average at about $4.17, down 12 cents from a week earlier.

Mon Nov 2policy

Teachers union sues Education Department over stalled student loan forgiveness buybacks

The American Federation of Teachers and nine borrowers have filed a proposed class action accusing the Education Department of stalling Public Service Loan Forgiveness decisions and stripping credit borrowers had earned toward forgiveness.

Fri Oct 30money

New I bonds will pay 5.51%, with the highest fixed rate since 2006

Series I savings bonds bought from Nov. 1 through April 30, 2027, will earn a 5.51% annual rate, up from 4.26% for bonds bought from May through October, the Treasury Department said Friday.

Fri Oct 30economy

Labor costs rise 0.8% in Q3 as inflation-adjusted wages fall 0.6% over the year

Compensation costs for U.S. civilian workers rose a seasonally adjusted 0.8% in the three months through September, after a 0.9% gain in the second quarter, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Friday.

Fri Oct 30policy

Social Security's revised heart-disability criteria take effect, adding three new listings

The Social Security Administration's revised medical criteria for judging disability claims involving heart and circulatory disorders took effect Friday, Oct. 30.

Thu Oct 29mortgages

30-year mortgage rate falls to 7.24%, a second weekly drop

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate fell to 7.24% this week from 7.32%, its second straight weekly decline and its lowest level this month, Freddie Mac said Thursday.

Thu Oct 29economy

Weekly jobless claims dip to 194,000 as continuing claims also fall

First-time claims for state unemployment benefits fell by 1,000 to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 in the week ended Oct. 24, the Labor Department said Thursday.

Wed Oct 28economy

Fed holds rates at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote, with two officials favoring a hike

The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark federal funds rate in a range of 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, with two of 12 voters dissenting in favor of a 0.25 percentage point increase.

Wed Oct 28mortgages

Mortgage applications rise 3.4% as 30-year rate dips to 7.37%

U.S. mortgage applications rose 3.4% in the week ending Oct. 23 as the average 30-year fixed rate fell to 7.37% from 7.41%, its lowest in three weeks, the Mortgage Bankers Association said Wednesday.

Tue Oct 27economy

Consumer confidence rebounds to 91.7 in October as gas prices ease

U.S. consumer confidence rose in October as gasoline prices eased, with The Conference Board's index climbing 7.5 points to 91.7 from an upwardly revised 84.2 in September.

Tue Oct 27economy

Case-Shiller: U.S. home prices up 2.1% from a year ago in August, trailing 3.4% inflation

U.S. home prices rose 2.1% in the year to August, up from a 1.9% gain in July, according to the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller national index released Tuesday.

Mon Oct 26regulation

FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General, alleging shoppers paid more than posted prices

The Federal Trade Commission and 20 states sued Dollar General on Monday, alleging the discount chain routinely charged customers more at the register than the prices shown on shelves, price tags and ads.

Mon Oct 26courts

Appeals court strikes down the Fed's 21-cent cap on debit card swipe fees

A federal appeals court ruled Monday that the Federal Reserve must rewrite its cap on what large banks may charge merchants to process debit card transactions, upholding a lower-court decision that threw out the 21-cent limit.

Sat Oct 24mortgages

Mortgage rates dip to 7.32%, Freddie Mac says

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate fell to 7.32% this week from 7.40%, according to Freddie Mac's weekly survey.

Fri Oct 23economy

Consumer sentiment holds at 48.0 as 85% say it's a bad time to buy a house

The University of Michigan's final October reading of consumer sentiment came in at 48.0, barely below September's 48.1 and down from 53.6 a year earlier.

Fri Oct 23policy

IRS creates a correction program for IRA errors, starting May 1, 2027

Treasury and the IRS created the IRA Compliance Resolution System, a program that lets IRA owners and custodians ask to fix certain mistakes caused by service providers.

Fri Oct 23regulation

Court bans debt-relief operators who targeted seniors and veterans, FTC says

A federal court entered a $106.8 million judgment against companies behind a debt-relief scheme that the FTC said impersonated banks, credit card companies and government agencies to target seniors and veterans.

Freddie Mac's weekly survey shows the average 30-year fixed rate fell to 7.32% from 7.40%, ending a seven-week run of increases.

modals.2026-10-22-money-1:
Thursday · Oct 22, 2026 · Money Digest · mortgages

30-year mortgage rate dips to 7.32%, first drop in 8 weeks

Freddie Mac's weekly survey shows the average 30-year fixed rate fell to 7.32% from 7.40%, ending a seven-week run of increases. The 15-year fixed rate slipped to 6.68% from 6.71%. A year ago, the two averaged 6.19% and 5.44%.

Why it matters: Mortgage rates track the 10-year Treasury yield, which eased this week. Even after the dip, rates sit more than a full point above last year's level, so monthly payments on a new loan remain well above what buyers faced a year ago.

References

  1. Mortgage Rates
    Freddie Mac · freddiemac.com · 2026-10-22
  2. Mortgage Rates Drop for First Time in 2 Months
    Realtor.com · realtor.com · 2026-10-22
  3. 30-year mortgage rate eases after seven-week climb
    Mortgage Professional America · mpamag.com · 2026-10-22
modals.2026-10-23-money-1:
Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · Money Digest · economy

Consumer sentiment holds at 48.0 as 85% say it's a bad time to buy a house

The University of Michigan's final October reading of consumer sentiment came in at 48.0, barely below September's 48.1 and down from 53.6 a year earlier. The survey found 85% of consumers said it is a bad time to buy a house, and 62% blamed high interest rates, up from 47% last month. The share who said high prices are hurting their personal finances rose for a fourth straight month, to 56%.

Why it matters: Survey director Joanne Hsu said buying conditions for big-ticket items fell on higher interest rates and affordability worries. About 69% of consumers expect interest rates to rise in the year ahead, the highest share since April 2023.

References

  1. As concerns over purchasing power dominate, consumer sentiment moves sideways
    University of Michigan · news.umich.edu · 2026-10-23
  2. UMich final October consumer sentiment 48.0
    investingLive · investinglive.com · 2026-10-23
modals.2026-10-23-money-2:
Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · Money Digest · policy

IRS creates a correction program for IRA errors, starting May 1, 2027

Treasury and the IRS created the IRA Compliance Resolution System, a program that lets IRA owners and custodians ask to fix certain mistakes caused by service providers. The program, required by the SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022, takes effect May 1, 2027. It will also take requests to waive the 60-day deadline for moving money from one plan or IRA into another, which today need a private letter ruling; that shift happens over 2027 and 2028. A second revenue procedure, effective Oct. 22, updates the existing correction program for employer retirement plans.

Why it matters: Until now IRA owners had no formal IRS program for fixing errors made by their providers, and 60-day rollover waivers required a private letter ruling. The existing automatic waiver and self-certification options stay available at no cost for those who qualify.

References

  1. Treasury, IRS update retirement plan correction program and establish correction program for individual retirement accounts
    IRS · irs.gov · 2026-10-23
  2. Revenue Procedure 2026-33: IRA Compliance Resolution System
    IRS · irs.gov · 2026-10-23
modals.2026-10-23-money-3:
Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · Money Digest · regulation

Court bans debt-relief operators who targeted seniors and veterans, FTC says

A federal court entered a $106.8 million judgment against companies behind a debt-relief scheme that the FTC said impersonated banks, credit card companies and government agencies to target seniors and veterans. The FTC said the October 14 order permanently bans the corporate and individual defendants from the debt-relief business and from telemarketing. The agency had alleged the operators falsely promised to cut consumers' debts by 75% or more and collected illegal advance fees. Money collected from the individual defendants would be available for consumer refunds.

Why it matters: The case involved callers posing as people's banks or government agencies. Besides the industry ban, the order bars the defendants from impersonating any government entity or business and from using consumers' credit reports without a permissible purpose.

References

  1. Court Permanently Shuts Down Illegal Debt Relief Operation Following FTC Allegation That Scheme's Operators Impersonated Government and Business Entities
    FTC · ftc.gov · 2026-10-23
modals.2026-10-24-wk-4:
Saturday · Oct 24, 2026 · Weekend Digest · mortgages

Mortgage rates dip to 7.32%, Freddie Mac says

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate fell to 7.32% in the week to Oct 22 from 7.40% a week earlier, Freddie Mac said. The 15-year fixed rate averaged 6.68%, down from 6.71%.
